subject: Proof-of-possession artifacts for VPC/on-prem KMS integration
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@securevault.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-health.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: VPC HSM attestation + PoP artifacts proposal

Hi Jasmine,

Following our demo last week, attaching a concise proposal for the "proof-of-possession" (PoP) artifacts we can provide from our on-prem HSM gateway to satisfy Acme's auditors and Redwood's security checklist. High-level summary:

- Attestation bundle (PDF) that includes a TPM-style quote from the HSM, vendor-signed firmware manifest, and a nonce-signed ephemeral key proof. See attached: sv-attestation-20280514.pdf.
- Short-lived wrapping keys: we propose issuing an HSM-wrapped ephemeral KEK (Key Encryption Key) per session (15 minute lifetime), signed by our hardware signing key.
- No plaintext egress: only wrapped blobs leave Acme VPC boundary; raw key material never traverses our network.
- Egress-minimization checklist (XLSX) enumerating telemetry we emit (metrics, attestation artifacts), and network flows needed for ledger and audit collection.

Technical asks for Redwood:
1) Confirm the exact KMS API call you expect for automatic wrap/unwrap in the private deployment (REST vs gRPC + auth header format).
2) Indicator whether Redwood will accept SHA-384 attestation signatures (our HSMs support RSA-3072 and ECDSA P-384).
3) Any constraints on the ephemeral key TTL we should enforce (we recommended 15 minutes but can go lower).

Open to a quick call tomorrow to walk through the bundle.

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Integrations Lead, SecureVault Inc.
attachments: sv-attestation-20280514.pdf, egress-checklist-v1.xlsx

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@securevault.com>
Cc: security@acme-health.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC HSM attestation + PoP artifacts proposal

Thanks Alice — this looks like a good starting point.

On Tue, May 14, 2028 at 9:15 AM Alice Zhang <alice@securevault.com> wrote:
> Following our demo last week, attaching a concise proposal for the "proof-of-possession" (PoP) artifacts we can provide ...

Couple of clarifying questions from our side before we schedule a walkthrough with Acme:
- Attestation artifact contents: can you include the exact structure of the nonce-signed bundle (JSON schema) and an example of the HSM quote? The PDF is helpful but auditors want a machine-parseable example.
- Wrap/unwrap flow: we need the sequence diagram for when the ephemeral KEK is generated in the HSM vs when Redwood issues the wrapping request from the private control plane. Can you attach a simple keyflow diagram (PNG is fine).
- Signature algorithms: we prefer ECDSA P-384 for smaller artifacts, but if RSA-3072 is what you recommend for compatibility we can accept it — confirm which you will sign the bundle with.
- Compliance ask from Acme: they require a TTL <= 30 minutes for ephemeral KEKs, and a rotation proof once per new deployment. Is 15 minutes acceptable to you (Alice stated 15)?

If you can provide the JSON schema and a keyflow PNG, we can run a short smoke-test in our staging private deploy next week.

I'll loop in our internal folks for specific owners.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Lead, Private Deployments (Redwood Inference)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice@securevault.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: SecureVault PoP bundle + next steps (Acme Health)

Team — forwarding SecureVault's proposal and Alice's attachments. TL;DR: vendor can provide hardware-signed attestation plus ephemeral wrapping keys; they claim no plaintext egress. We need to validate artifacts and decide acceptance criteria.

Quick owners and asks:
- Stephanie: own artifact intake and evidence (attestation PDF + machine JSON schema). Put together an "artifact acceptance checklist" for Acme auditors (deadline: EOD 5/15). Attachments: egress-checklist-v1.xlsx.
- Rishi: crypto/operations review. Confirm we can accept ECDSA P-384 bundles and review the nonce flow for replay protection. Also define expected logging/telemetry footprint inside our private control plane.
- Vanessa: network & VPC guardrails. Validate that the vendor's network flows in the checklist (outbound to ledger endpoints) fit our minimal egress policy; propose firewall rules and private endpoints for HSM attestation.
- Karthik: update our KMS SDK adapter to accept a wrapped-KEK blob from vendor and implement the short-lived unwrap handshake (target patch for 5/21).

We should run a smoke test in staging the week of 5/20. Proposed meeting to align and confirm acceptance criteria:
- Proposed: Thu 5/16 11:00-11:30am PT (30m)

Notes: include the following acceptance gates for the PoP bundle: machine-parseable quote (JSON), vendor-signed firmware manifest, signed ephemeral KEK metadata (TTL + nonce), and evidence that no plaintext private keys are exported.

Attachments referenced: sv-attestation-20280514.pdf, egress-checklist-v1.xlsx, PoP-keyflow-diagram.png

-Jasmine
